title: Beyond Performance: Does Assessed Potential Matter to Employees' Voluntary Departure Decisions?

scopes.description: Complete supplied author-documented raw-to-final dataset workflow using both Stata programs; this scope ends at the analysis-ready Analysis_Data_FINAL.dta file and does not claim to estimate the paper's tables.

requirements.description: Annual year-end employee records for management levels 1-5, 2008-2015. Code 1 normalizes varying workbook headers into a PersonID-Year panel with demographics, management/employment history, country/region, unit/function, supervisors, compensation and performance fields. The workbook's performance rating for calendar-year snapshot t is for t-1; 2015 supplies 2014 ratings, not 2015 ratings.

issues.description: The package contains code and documentation but not the private personnel workbooks. The NDA statement establishes that the authors cannot share their underlying data; it does not establish that this user lacks an authorized compatible source. Current access, identifiers, exact source fields and histories therefore remain unverified.

Both supplied Code 2 programs use the same author project root. Program 19 writes Processed_Data_2.dta under Beyond Performance Project/JAR Data; Program 20 reads the same basename under Beyond Performance/JAR Data, omitting the Project segment. The producer-consumer identity and order are supported. In an isolated working copy, map the shared project root to a host-visible writable [redacted-path-ba60ef031de2] root and align Program 20's read directory with Program 19's output directory, preserving the separate Data Received, JAR Data, Data Processing_Validity Testing and code directories. This is a known path-configuration preparation step; no old-machine alias needs proof.

The Code 1 import path for the required updated 2010-2014 ratings retains the literal [HR contact last name] filename placeholder. Resolve it only against an already-authorized local source; do not infer a real name or request contact.

For raw Excel inputs, the author documents a manual copy/save-as step that removes the workbook-open protection before Stata imports the files. No such data workbook is packaged, and the environment probe does not confirm Excel availability; if the current compatible source is already in the required importable form, this step may not apply.
